findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block, committing long-lived static credentials to source control and exposing them to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or console read access.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the Lambda environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in cleartext by any principal able to describe the function, with no separate key policy boundary.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet controls, easing data exfiltration if the function or its embedded credentials are abused.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so unsigned or tampered deployment packages can be published to the function without integrity verification.
